query: If the most common hardware failure causes were addressed, how much would the hardware incident rate drop?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes hardware from other categories; the query is about hardware incidents, so this scoping variable is implied by the query text. Not a settable lever.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Identifies the specific hardware failure causes (connectivity, drive failure, overheating, etc.). This is exactly the 'most common failure causes' the query proposes to address. However, a failure mode is a diagnostic classification of what went wrong, not itself a directly settable lever; addressing it requires an unspecified upstream intervention.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident recurs is a downstream manifestation of the incident rate itself, not a common cause of treatment and outcome. Behaves as an outcome/proxy rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs production vs shared) plausibly influences both which failure modes occur and the incident rate/visibility, and is not named in the query. Weak-to-moderate confounder.

per_column.name: software_issue_subtype
per_column.rationale: Pertains to software incidents, largely NULL for hardware; irrelevant to the hardware outcome and not a common cause of the hardware failure treatment.

judge.rationale: The added columns identify the 'treatment' (failure_mode = the common hardware failure causes) and scope it to hardware, matching the query's framing. But the what-if claim fails on both prongs. (a) failure_mode is a diagnostic label of what failed, not an intervenable lever an actor can set/change/decide; the query's 'addressed' action (e.g., a maintenance policy, hardware replacement program, patch schedule) is nowhere represented as a settable treatment. (b) No genuine confounder that is a common cause of BOTH an intervention and the hardware incident rate is provided: incident_category and failure_mode are query-implied scoping/treatment, recurrence_signal is an outcome/proxy, software_issue_subtype is irrelevant, and only affected_scope is a plausible not-named confounder — and even it is weak and not clearly a common cause of an intervention. The set does not set up an identifiable counterfactual effect of an intervenable treatment.
